title: A platform package deleted by `git add -A` would land on dev: lore's set-comparison runs only on a release dispatch, never on a PR
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-15, prompted by a REAL incident in quest-cli rather than a hypothetical. WHAT HAPPENED TO QUEST, in their words and their measurement. A tracker-only PR -- one .quest/ file -- went red reproducibly on their source-gates job: git diff --stat 66a7f7d 67be2b7 -- npm/ npm/quest-darwin-arm64/LICENSE | 21 ----- npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest | Bin 64634978 -> 0 bytes npm/quest-darwin-arm64/package.json | 21 ----- Those files were absent from the working tree when `git add -A` ran. Nothing in the session touched them. `git add -A` STAGES A DELETION FOR A TRACKED FILE THAT IS MERELY MISSING, so the commit deleted an entire platform package. Afterwards the index matched the working tree, so `git status` reported CLEAN and `git diff HEAD -- npm/` was EMPTY. Every command anyone would reach for said nothing was wrong. Their commit message and PR body both said "tracker-only" and both were false. Their scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs:19 caught it -- readdir(npm) returned 5 against 6 declared optionalDependencies. WHAT THIS REPOSITORY WOULD HAVE DONE: LANDED IT. ci.yml -> no reference to npm/ anywhere. No PR-time check. package.json scripts -> no check:packages, no equivalent. release.yml:134-141 -> DOES compare the declared platform set against root optionalDependencies keys... but release.yml is `on: workflow_dispatch` ONLY (line 14-15), so it never fires on a push, a PR, or a tag. So lore has the right check and runs it at the wrong time. A platform package silently deleted by `git add -A` on a tracker-only commit would pass every gate on the PR, land on dev, and first be detected during a RELEASE DISPATCH. That is the precise failure mode CLAUDE.md warns about: "a gate that is wrong fails only during a release." Worse, the detection would arrive at the moment it is most expensive and most likely to be misread. A release operator seeing "platform set mismatch" mid-dispatch has to decide whether the release machinery is broken or the repository is, under time pressure, with the tag possibly already cut. MY OWN TREE IS INTACT, checked rather than assumed: npm/ holds 6 directories, each containing exactly package.json. git ls-tree -r v0.7.0 -- npm/ shows the same 6 files -- package.json only. git diff --stat 41ac5a65 HEAD -- npm/ is empty: nothing today touched it. Note the design difference that makes lore's surface SMALLER but not safer: lore does not commit platform binaries (they are built in CI), so each npm// holds one file where quest's holds three including a 64MB binary. Fewer files to lose, and the same `git add -A` mechanism loses them just as silently. A smaller blast radius is not a guard. THIS IS ALSO THE DECLARED-SUBJECT CLAUSE OF THE SHIPPED-README CONTRACT, ARRIVING FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION. That clause was argued on a file APPEARING in a package directory and changing A1's subject silently. Quest's incident is a file DISAPPEARING from a tree that reports clean. A discovered set changes membership in both directions and neither is announced; an enumerated one does not. Their closed `files` list is what made the drift detectable, and it detected a case neither of us imagined when arguing for it. REMEDY, and the cheap version is genuinely cheap: 1. A `check:packages` script asserting readdir(npm/) equals the root optionalDependencies key set, plus each npm/

/package.json being present and parseable. Wire it into ci.yml so it runs on every PR. 2. Give each npm//package.json an explicit `files` list. They currently have NONE, so npm packs whatever the directory contains -- today exactly package.json, but the set is discovered rather than declared. This is the same clause as the README contract's A1 and should land with it. 3. Consider moving release.yml's existing set-comparison into the shared script so there is ONE assertion invoked from two places, rather than two that can disagree. CREDIT WHERE IT IS DUE: this gap was not found by inspection here. quest-cli hit the real thing, reported it against its own interest, and I checked whether lore would have caught it. It would not have.
implementationNotes:
SESSION HANDOFF 2026-09-15. FILED, UNSTARTED. Nothing has been implemented; the description holds the full measurement.

WHY IT IS HIGH AND SHOULD NOT BE DEFERRED BEHIND THE README WORK: the failure is
SILENT and lands on dev. `git add -A` stages a deletion for any tracked file merely
MISSING from the tree, and afterwards the index matches the tree -- so `git status`
reports clean and `git diff HEAD` is empty. Every command anyone would reach for
confirms nothing is wrong. quest-cli lost an entire platform package this way on a
tracker-only PR whose message said "tracker-only" and was false.

THE EXPOSURE IS STRUCTURAL HERE, not incidental: `git add -A .quest` is MANDATORY
in this repository because `quest complete` renames tasks/ -> completed/ and a bare
`git add` leaves a dangling delete. So the flag this repo requires is the flag that
launders an unrelated deletion into a tracker commit. quest-cli has offered to file
a quest-side change where `quest complete` stages its own rename, which would let a
scoped `git add .quest` suffice; that offer is open and unanswered.

INTERIM DISCIPLINE, already in use in this session's later commits and worth
keeping until the check exists: scope the stage (`git add -A .quest`, never bare
`git add -A`) and read `git diff --cached --name-status` before committing. A
"tracker-only" claim is checkable in one command.

STATE VERIFIED AT HANDOFF, so the successor need not re-derive it:
  npm/ holds 6 dirs, each containing exactly package.json
  git ls-tree -r v0.7.0 -- npm/  shows the same 6 files
  git diff --stat 41ac5a65 HEAD -- npm/  is empty
  npm/*/package.json have NO `files` field -- npm packs whatever the dir holds
  .gitignore includes `npm/*/bin/`, so built binaries would be ignored if present
The tree is intact. This is a missing GATE, not an active corruption.

DESIGN NOTE THAT IS EASY TO MISREAD AS SAFETY: lore builds platform binaries in CI
rather than committing them, so each dir holds one file where quest's holds three.
That is a smaller blast radius, NOT a guard.

REMEDY, in the description, unchanged: a check:packages script asserting
readdir(npm/) equals the root optionalDependencies key set, wired into ci.yml so it
runs on every PR; explicit `files` lists on each platform package.json; and ideally
ONE shared assertion invoked from both ci.yml and release.yml rather than two that
can disagree. release.yml:134-141 already has the comparison -- it is
`on: workflow_dispatch` only, which is the entire defect.

PROOF, per the fleet rule and this session's own experience with clause 3: prove
rejection AND acceptance as two separate measurements -- delete a platform dir and
see the new job go red for ITS OWN reason (read the message, not just the colour),
then restore and see the tree green. Confirm the other jobs are green on both SHAs.
